pk.context: 25 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: Bioavailability is about 15%, mostly lost to presystemic metabolism. Protein binding is low, about 14% to 21%, and a high-fat meal raises Cmax and AUC by 15% and 12%.
clues.substance: Supplied as the succinate salt; the active moiety has a molecular weight of 295.4 and is readily soluble in water and saline.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA in 25, 50 and 100 mg tablets.
clues.safety: No boxed warning. Contraindicated in ischemic coronary artery disease, prior stroke or TIA, and uncontrolled hypertension; atypical sensations and paresthesia are reported.
clues.indication: Acute treatment of migraine with or without aura in adults.
clues.mechanism: A selective agonist at 5-HT1B/1D receptors on intracranial blood vessels and trigeminal nerves, causing vessel constriction and inhibiting pro-inflammatory neuropeptide release.

tell: Only about 15% of an oral tablet reaches the circulation, mostly lost to first-pass metabolism.
